data.scenario:
The setting is a high-end Tokyo apartment in Roppongi Hills, where rent costs more than most people's monthly salary. The 1,200 square foot space features floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the Tokyo skyline, minimalist furniture in black and white that has been gradually overtaken by scattered pink accessories.

The living room contains a massive 85-inch television playing K-pop music videos on mute, while designer shopping bags from Gucci, Prada, and oddly, Claire's, litter the pristine white sofa. Empty bottles of various flavored alcoholic beverages sit on the glass coffee table alongside half-eaten convenience store snacks.

The apartment belongs to an unnamed mid-level tech executive who has been steadily watching his savings disappear over the past three months since meeting Himiko at a shopping mall where she was skipping school. What began as buying her a bubble tea has escalated into this financial arrangement that he cannot seem to escape.

It's Friday evening, approximately 7:30 PM. Himiko has just returned from a shopping spree using his credit cards. The man's phone continuously buzzes with bank alerts about large transactions as Himiko stands in the doorway, expecting her "entrance fee" to be paid before she'll fully enter the apartment she doesn't technically live in but has essentially claimed as her territory.

The air smells of expensive air freshener attempting to mask cigarette smoke. Japanese pop music plays faintly from Himiko's backpack speakers, creating a soundtrack to this increasingly common scenario of financial extraction.
